title: Nature's Tangent Line or Adaptationist Mirage?: Optimal Foraging Theory and the Marginal Value Theorem on Trial — From MacArthur & Pianka's 1966 zero-one prey-choice inequality & Charnov's 1976 parameter-free Marginal Value Theorem tangent rule to Cowie's 1977 sawdust-cup great tits & Hayden, Pearson & Platt's 2011 macaque anterior cingulate integrate-to-threshold ramps; adversarial cross-examination via Pierce & Ollason's 1987 Oikos broadside, Kacelnik & Bateson's Weber-law delay risk-proneness, Nonacs's 26-study predation overstaying audit, Joel Brown's Giving-Up Density & Simpson-Raubenheimer Nutritional Geometry

teenKit.tldr: Animals, humans, and doom-scrollers all face the same ancient mathematical trap: figuring out the exact split-second to stop digging into a draining resource and move on to a fresh one.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This exact biological calculus explains everything from how a wild wolf breaks off a hunt to why you can't close TikTok at 2:00 AM.
keyTakeaways: Optimal Foraging Theory uses hard math to predict how animals make life-or-death economic choices about food and energy.
Eric Charnov's Marginal Value Theorem claims animals leave a patch the exact moment their intake rate drops to the average of the whole environment.
Real brains are messier than chalkboard math, relying on psychological quirks, time perception errors, and the constant fear of getting eaten.

vocab.meaning: A mathematical rule predicting that you should abandon a shrinking resource the moment your current gain drops below the global average.
The fundamental economic puzzle of deciding which available options to consume and which ones to completely ignore.
The universal tension between milking a known resource dry versus gambling on the unknown search for a better one.
A deceptive illusion where scientists assume every biological trait is a flawless mathematical optimization when it's actually just a messy evolutionary compromise.

quiz.question: According to Eric Charnov's Marginal Value Theorem, when is the optimal moment for an organism to leave a food patch?
options: When the patch is completely 100% empty of all resources
When the local intake rate drops down to match the habitat-wide average
When a predator is spotted within a 10-meter radius
When the animal gets tired and needs to take a nap
quiz.explanation: The tangent rule dictates departure precisely when the marginal return inside the patch matches the background average of the environment.

quiz.question: What common modern human behavior shares the exact same biological roots as an animal foraging in a patch?
options: Buying a brand new pair of sneakers online
Mindlessly scrolling through a social media feed or debug log
Sleeping for eight hours straight without waking up
Drinking a glass of cold water after running a marathon
quiz.explanation: Staring at a draining search page or social media feed is a direct modern parallel to the patch departure explore-exploit dilemma.

quiz.question: Why do real-world animals often overstay their welcome in a patch instead of following the strict mathematical optimum?
options: They are all mathematically trained by nature
They have infinite energy and never get tired
They factor in survival risks like predators and time-perception quirks
They prefer eating lower-quality food on purpose
quiz.explanation: Real biology introduces messy variables like the fear of predators and timing psychophysics that pull animals away from pristine chalkboard math.
